ar_crystal_cave.blurb: Crystal Cave is a small limestone bluff in northwest Arkansas, near Decatur, built around one big roof. It is a local bouldering spot rather than a trip destination, but it holds 14 problems and a decent share of them are hard: a handful of easier lines from V1 to V4, then most of the rest between V5 and V7. The roof has good rock and movement once the holds are brushed, though ledges can be dirty and some large flakes sound hollow, so test them before pulling. A trail runs along the bluff past more caves, and the page notes room for further problems and linkups.

ar_seed_wall.blurb: Seed Wall is one of the walls of The Outback, the section of Sam's Throne in north-central Arkansas reached by the Dog Walkdown. The 14 climbs are mostly traditional, with a few sport and top-rope lines mixed in, and the wall is known above all for crack climbing in several sizes and angles. Grades start around 5.5 and top out near 5.11, with the bulk of the routes landing between 5.7 and 5.10, so it suits a leader who wants moderate crack practice as well as a couple of harder options. The rock is good on most lines.

ar_loaf_boulder.blurb: Loaf Boulder is a bouldering spot on the west side of Horseshoe Canyon Ranch in north-central Arkansas, in the southern part of the Idaho Boulders near the Confederate cracks. It holds 14 problems, and the spread is wide: several at the easy end from VB to V2, a middle group around V4, and a few real tests from V6 up to V8. One of its lines is a low traverse that finishes into a neighbouring problem, and a pad or two is recommended there. Good for a mixed group that wants both warm-ups and hard projects on one block.

ar_fire_wall_the.blurb: The Fire Wall is a steep sport wall at Rock Creek, a secluded cliff band in the Big Piney region of north-central Arkansas. All 14 routes are bolted and the climbing is demanding: a few at 5.10, a couple at 5.11, six at 5.12 and three at 5.13, so this is a wall for people already climbing the double digits. The face stays in shade for most of the day and keeps dry in a rainstorm. Expect powerful, overhanging movement typical of the creek's cliffs, with walls nearby that offer easier warm-ups.

ar_spivey_wall.blurb: Spivey Wall is a bolted wall at Rock Creek, a remote cliff band in the Big Piney region of north-central Arkansas. It has 14 sport routes with a strong middle: seven in the 5.11 range, four at 5.12, a pair at 5.10 and one 5.13. That makes it a good stop for someone stepping up from 5.10 into harder terrain, since there are warm-ups for the harder lines close by. Rock Creek climbing in general is steep and powerful, and the cliffs here run 50 to 80 feet tall, so expect sustained pulling rather than slabby balance.
